title: GKE Node Pool Autoscaling and Upgrade Events

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `google:gcp:pubsub:message` events with `resource.type="k8s_cluster" textPayload=*"upgrade"*` into `index=gcp`. Confirm UC-4.3.14 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `google:gcp:pubsub:message` traffic without `resource.type="k8s_cluster" textPayload=*"upgrade"*`. Confirm UC-4.3.14 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=gcp` sourcetype=`google:gcp:pubsub:message` collected via `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" resource.type="k8s_cluster" textPayload=*"upgrade"*
| table _time messageId publishTime attributes
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.14_gke_node_pool_autoscalin_14"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.3.14 — GKE Node Pool Autoscaling and Upgrade Events: queries Google Cloud `google:gcp:pubsub:message` for search criteria `resource.type="k8s_cluster" textPayload=*"upgrade"*` and returns actor, resource, and region context for availability review and change validation.
value: On Google Cloud, detecting 'GKE Node Pool Autoscaling and Upgrade Events' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.3.14 drives high-priority availability alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Ingest GKE logs (cluster operations, node pool events). Monitor node count and autoscaler events. Track upgrade and maintenance window events. Alert on node pool scaling failures.
visualization: Timeline (node pool events), Table (cluster, pool, node count), Line chart (node count over time).
knownFalsePositives: During a roll-out, nodes come and go and metrics briefly look off. We ignore short windows that line up with a deployment and we focus on steady-state failures after the cluster is calm again.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=gcp`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` with the modular input for `google:gcp:pubsub:message`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.3.41.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `messageId` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest GKE logs (cluster operations, node pool events). Monitor node count and autoscaler events. Track upgrade and maintenance window events. Alert on node pool scaling failures.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" resource.type="k8s_cluster" textPayload=*"upgrade"*
| table _time messageId publishTime attributes
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.14_gke_node_pool_autoscalin_14"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `google:gcp:pubsub:message` in `index=gcp` to detect gke node pool autoscaling and upgrade events. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `messageId` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_3_14_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Timeline (node pool events), Table (cluster, pool, node count), Line chart (node count over time)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of gke node pool autoscaling and upgrade events so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
